formation.title: The Founding of Mossi
formation.text:
The scattered Mossi kingdoms have been united under a single banner. From the Volta headwaters to the edges of the Sahel, the descendants of Ouédraogo now speak with one voice. But what kind of nation shall we forge from this union? The Nakomsé warrior aristocracy stands ready to ride, their cavalry the terror of Mali and Songhai alike. Yet the Mogho Naba's court in Ouagadougou offers another path, the sacred institution of naam, the elaborate hierarchy of provincial nabas and village chiefs, a system of governance that has endured for centuries through wisdom rather than conquest alone.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Let the hooves of our horses shake the earth!

modifiers.name: Riders of the Naam
modifiers.text: The divine power of naam courses through the veins of our horsemen. The Nakomsé cavalry tradition, passed from father to son since the founders rode north from Mamprusi, defines our strength. No empire of the Sahel can match the thunder of our mounted warriors across the grasslands.

options.text: The Mogho Naba's wisdom shall guide our people.

modifiers.name: The Mogho Naba's Court
modifiers.text: The Mogho Naba sits at the apex of a hierarchy that radiates from Ouagadougou to every village. His ministers, the Ouidi Naba commanding cavalry, the Baloum Naba overseeing stewardship, the Larlé Naba guarding royal customs, form an administration of remarkable sophistication for the Sahel.

advances.name: Nakomsé Horsemanship
advances.text: The cavalry traditions of the Nakomsé warrior aristocracy, who trace their lineage to the founding horsemen from Mamprusi.

event.title: The Nakomsé Ride Forth
event.text: The Nakomsé horsemen have formalized their ancient cavalry traditions into a disciplined fighting force. Since the founding ancestors rode north from the Mamprusi lands, mounted warfare has been the birthright of the Mossi ruling class. Now, with proper training grounds and breeding programs, our cavalry strikes fear into the hearts of neighboring kingdoms. The thunder of hooves across the savanna is the sound of Mossi power.

options.text: The naam gives us the right to ride and to rule.

advances.name: Earth Shrine Tradition
advances.text: The ancient practice of maintaining sacred earth shrines tended by tengsoba priests, binding the community to the spiritual power of the land.

event.title: The Earth Shrines Speak
event.text: The tengbiise, the original inhabitants of our lands, have renewed the ancient covenant between people and soil. In every village, the tengsoba earth priest tends the sacred groves where the spirits of the land dwell. These shrines predate even the Nakomsé conquest, and their power remains essential to Mossi life. The earth grants fertility to our fields, protection to our villages, and spiritual authority that complements the political power of the nabas. While Islamic influence creeps in from the north, our earth shrines stand as bastions of ancestral tradition.

options.text: The earth spirits guard our way of life.

modifiers.name: Earth Shrine Awakening
modifiers.text: The tengsoba earth priests have renewed their bond with the land. The ancient shrines of the tengbiise pulse with spiritual power, protecting our people from foreign religions and binding the community to the soil that sustains them.

advances.name: Ironworking Lineages
advances.text: The feared blacksmith castes of the Mossi, whose mastery of iron smelting and forging is considered both essential and spiritually dangerous.

advances.name: Volta Agriculture
advances.text: Intensive cultivation of millet, sorghum, and other crops in the fertile Volta River headwaters region. In the dry north the crusted ground is opened with planting pits before the rains.

advances.name: Naba Hierarchy
advances.text: The tiered system of provincial nabas, district chiefs, and village nabas that transmits the Mogho Naba's authority throughout the realm.

advances.name: Cotton Weaving
advances.text: The traditional strip-loom weaving of cotton cloth, where women spin and dye the thread while men weave it into the distinctive Mossi textiles.

advances.name: Lancer Tradition
advances.text: Professional mounted warriors armed with iron-tipped lances forged by Mossi blacksmiths, the heavy arm of the Nakomsé cavalry.

advances.name: Sacred Kingship
advances.text: The institution of naam, the divine authority to rule, and the elaborate court of the Mogho Naba with its six powerful ministers.

event.title: The Sacred Institution of Naam
event.text: The Mogho Naba has completed the transformation of Mossi governance into a system of sacred kingship unmatched in the Sahel. The power of naam, the divine authority to rule, flows from the Mogho Naba through the provincial nabas to the village chiefs, creating an unbroken chain of legitimate authority. The daily false departure ceremony, where the Mogho Naba mounts his horse as if to abandon his people before being persuaded to stay, reminds all that the king's commitment to his subjects is renewed each morning.

options.text: The naam endures, and so shall our kingdom.

advances.name: Resistance to Mali
advances.text: The Mossi kingdoms' defiant resistance against the Mali Empire, raiding its caravans and garrisons rather than submitting to its authority. Behind the horsemen the commoners march on foot with their bows.

advances.name: Horse Rearing
advances.text: Specialized breeding programs that produce the hardy horses essential to Mossi cavalry dominance across the Sahel grasslands.

advances.name: Sahel Trade Network
advances.text: A network of markets and caravanserais linking Mossi lands to the trans-Saharan trade routes, exchanging cotton, cattle, and grain for salt and luxury goods.

event.title: Crossroads of the Sahel
event.text: Mossi traders have established a network of caravanserais linking our markets to the great trans-Saharan routes. Cotton cloth woven on our strip looms, cattle from our herds, and millet from our fields flow northward, while salt, kola nuts, and luxury goods travel south through our territory. By taxing and protecting these trade routes, the Mossi have become essential middlemen in the commerce of the western Sahel, growing prosperous without the wars of conquest that consumed Mali and Songhai.

options.text: Our markets shall be the meeting place of nations.

advances.name: Provincial Courts
advances.text: The system of regional governance where provincial nabas hold court, administering justice and collecting tribute with considerable local autonomy.

advances.name: Iron Guard Tradition
advances.text: Elite infantry armed with weapons of superior Mossi iron, trained to hold ground while the cavalry maneuvers.

advances.name: Songhai Defiance
advances.text: The stubborn Mossi resistance to Songhai expansion, fortifying villages and using knowledge of the terrain to offset the larger empire's military advantages.

advances.name: Mask Artistry
advances.text: The distinctive tall masks of the Mossi, carved to honor ancestors and nature spirits, used in festivals and ceremonies that bind communities together.

advances.name: Trade Caravans
advances.text: Organized trading expeditions that carry Mossi goods across the Sahel, establishing diplomatic relationships alongside commercial ones.

advances.name: Ancestor Veneration
advances.text: The deepening of ancestral worship practices, where offerings at patrilineal shrines connect the living to the wisdom and protection of their forebears.

advances.name: Dolo Tradition
advances.text: The communal brewing of dolo, millet beer that serves as both a staple beverage and a centerpiece of social and religious gatherings.

advances.name: Fortified Villages
advances.text: The practice of surrounding villages with defensive walls and ditches, creating a network of strongpoints across Mossi territory.

advances.name: Sahel Riders
advances.text: Mounted warriors adapted to the full range of Sahel terrain, equally at home in grassland and scrubland, with tactics refined through centuries of border warfare.

advances.name: Naam Consolidation
advances.text: The strengthening of the Mogho Naba's sacred authority, centralizing the institution of naam to create more effective governance across the united kingdoms.

advances.name: Gold Dust Trade
advances.text: Mossi merchants gain access to the gold dust trade flowing from southern mines through their territory, enriching the kingdom's treasury.

advances.name: Indigo Dyeing
advances.text:
The mastery of indigo dyeing techniques that transform Mossi cotton cloth into prized trade goods sought across West Africa.

Available in: Weaving House

advances.name: False Departure Ceremony
advances.text: The daily ritual where the Mogho Naba mounts his horse as if to depart, only to be persuaded to stay, a powerful symbol of the covenant between ruler and people.

advances.name: Regional Autonomy
advances.text: The careful balance between central authority and provincial autonomy that has allowed the Mossi kingdoms to govern diverse peoples without provoking rebellion.

advances.name: Naam Cavalry
advances.text: The last great evolution of Mossi mounted warfare, combining traditional horsemanship with modern tactical discipline under the naam authority.

advances.name: Mogho Naba Reforms
advances.text: Administrative reforms that modernize the Mossi state while preserving the essential institutions of naam and the sacred authority of the Mogho Naba.

advances.name: Sahel Diplomacy
advances.text: A sophisticated diplomatic tradition developed through centuries of navigating between larger empires, maintaining independence through alliance-building and shrewd negotiation.

advances.name: Cotton Exports
advances.text:
The expansion of Mossi cotton cloth production from local trade to major export commodity, with strip-woven textiles reaching markets across the Sahel and beyond.

Available in: Weaving House

advances.name: Warrior Aristocracy
advances.text: The Nakomsé warrior class has refined its martial traditions into a professional military establishment, combining noble cavalry traditions with disciplined training.

advances.name: Mossi Jurisprudence
advances.text: The codification of Mossi legal traditions, drawing on the dual sources of political authority from the nabas and spiritual authority from the tengsoba earth priests.

advances.name: Modern Horsemen
advances.text: The adaptation of Mossi cavalry to the modern age, combining traditional grassland mobility with contemporary military organization. A standing body of horse is kept under the Ouidi Naba.

advances.name: Mossi Renaissance
advances.text: A flowering of Mossi intellectual life, as traditional knowledge systems engage with new ideas flowing along the trade routes of the Sahel.

advances.name: Sahel Confederation
advances.text: The vision of a broader Sahel political union, extending the Mossi model of federated governance to neighboring peoples under a shared framework.

advances.name: Industrial Weaving
advances.text:
The mechanization of the ancient strip-loom tradition, transforming Mossi cotton weaving from a village craft into an industrial enterprise.

Available in: Weaving House

advances.name: Lasting Traditions
advances.text: The remarkable persistence of Mossi cultural traditions, the masks, the earth shrines, the naam, the daily ceremonies, enduring through centuries of change and external pressure.

advances.name: Volta Breadbasket
advances.text: The transformation of the Volta headwaters into a major agricultural region, feeding a growing population through intensified farming and improved techniques.

destiny.name: Mossi Destiny
destiny.text: The Mossi kingdoms stand united. Whether through the thunder of cavalry or the wisdom of the Mogho Naba's court, a greater destiny awaits the children of Ouédraogo.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Path of Mossi Destiny
event.text: The Mossi kingdoms have achieved a unity that our ancestors only dreamed of. From the halls of Ouagadougou to the provincial courts of Yatenga and Tenkodogo, the power of naam binds us together. Now the question is not whether we shall endure, the Mossi have always endured, but how we shall grow. Our destiny lies before us, waiting to be shaped by the choices of this generation.

options.text: The naam shall guide us to greatness.

destiny.name: Sahel Vanguard
destiny.text: Conquer the Dagomba lands to the south, securing the gateway cities of Yendi and Salaga for the Mossi cavalry. Fill the war chest for the campaigns to come.

conditions.text: Chose Riders of the Naam
Own Yendi, or a subject owns it
Own Salaga, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 1000

event.title: The Dagomba Submit
event.text: The thunder of Mossi cavalry has echoed across the southern grasslands. The Dagomba kingdom, whose warriors once contested our passage, now bows before the power of the Nakomsé. The markets of Yendi and Salaga, rich in kola nuts and trade connections to the forest kingdoms, now feed our war machine. Our horsemen range freely from the Volta headwaters to the edge of the forest belt. The first blow has been struck; the Niger Bend beckons.

options.text: Our hooves shall carry us further still.

destiny.name: Niger Campaign
destiny.text: Push north to seize the wealthy trading city of Djenné and the Niger River crossing at Say. The treasures of the Niger Bend await those bold enough to take them.

conditions.text: Own Djenné, or a subject owns it
Own Say, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 2000
Prestige at least 50

event.title: The Niger Bend Falls
event.text: Djenné, the jewel of the Niger, has fallen to Mossi arms. Our cavalry, descendants of the warriors who raided Mali's caravans for centuries, have at last seized the prize their ancestors could only plunder. The great mud-brick mosque looks down upon Mossi banners, and the river trade that once enriched Songhai now flows through our hands. How shall we consolidate this conquest?

options.text: Strike fast, strike hard. The Sahel fears us!

modifiers.name: Sahel Thunder
modifiers.text: The mere rumor of Mossi cavalry on the march sends enemies scrambling to fortify their cities. War comes swiftly, though the cost of maintaining such a fearsome reputation strains the treasury.

options.text: Our riders are our legacy, strength in the saddle.

modifiers.name: Raider Legacy
modifiers.text: The Mossi horsemen maintain the raiding tradition of their Nakomsé ancestors, reinforcing quickly and sustaining campaigns far from home through efficient foraging.

destiny.name: War Camp of the Naam
destiny.text: Complete the conquest of the Niger Bend by taking Timbuktu and Gao, the legendary cities that once served as capitals of Mali and Songhai. With these prizes in hand, the Mossi cavalry empire shall surpass all that came before.

conditions.text: Own Timbuktu, or a subject owns it
Own Gao, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75

event.title: Masters of the Niger
event.text: Timbuktu and Gao, the twin pillars of Sahel civilization, now answer to the Mogho Naba. What the empires of Mali and Songhai built over centuries, the Mossi cavalry has claimed in a generation. The trans-Saharan caravans that once carried salt and gold through foreign kingdoms now pass under our protection. Scholars in Timbuktu's madrasas write of the Mossi with the same awe once reserved for Mansa Musa. How shall we rule this vast domain?

options.text: We are the hegemony. All bow before the naam.

modifiers.name: Niger Hegemony
modifiers.text: The Mossi cavalry has proven it can take any city in the Sahel. Our ability to storm fortifications and dictate peace terms reflects the overwhelming military superiority of the naam.

options.text: We are the empire. All serve the Mossi banner.

modifiers.name: Sahel Empire
modifiers.text: A vast empire stretching across the Sahel, maintained by a professional army and mercenary auxiliaries. The cost of maintaining so many diplomatic ties pales beside the military strength gained.

destiny.name: Court Foundation
destiny.text: Establish the Mogho Naba's court as the center of a prosperous realm. Secure salt for the markets and build up Ouagadougou, the seat of the Mogho Naba.

conditions.text: Chose The Mogho Naba's Court
A market the country is in

children.text: Salt is produced in the market
Salt is traded in the market

conditions.text: Owns Ouagadougou with at least 19 development

event.title: The Court Takes Root
event.text: The Mogho Naba's vision of a prosperous, well-ordered realm is beginning to bear fruit. Salt caravans arrive regularly at our markets, bringing the essential commodity that preserves food and enables long-distance trade. Ouagadougou has outgrown the compound of the naba, and new wards spread around the court. The dual authority of political naam and spiritual earth-priest power creates a stability that neighboring kingdoms envy. This is governance as the ancestors intended.

options.text: Prosperity grows where good governance takes root.

destiny.name: Naam Institutions
destiny.text: Extend the court's commercial reach to the gold-trading city of Begho, and set the looms of three towns weaving the strip cloth its traders carry south. The Naam system provides stability; now it must also provide prosperity.

conditions.text: Gold at least 2000
Own Begho, or a subject owns it
A Weaving House stands in at least 3 of our locations

event.title: The Naam Embraces Commerce
event.text: The ancient institution of naam has proven remarkably adaptable. What began as a divine mandate to rule has expanded into a framework for economic governance. Mossi merchants, operating under the protection and regulation of the naba hierarchy, have established permanent trading relationships reaching as far south as the gold-rich forests of Begho. The court's hold on the looms and the Begho trade has not diminished its sacred character, rather, it has demonstrated that wisdom and wealth need not be rivals.

options.text: Trade shall flow through the channels of naam.

modifiers.name: Naam Prosperity
modifiers.text: The Mogho Naba's wise governance has created a flourishing trade network. Merchants prosper under stable policies, and the kingdom's sound financial practices keep inflation in check.

options.text: The court's wisdom attracts all who seek order.

modifiers.name: Court Wisdom
modifiers.text: The sophistication of the Mossi court system allows for the peaceful absorption of neighboring peoples through diplomacy rather than war. Favorable peace terms reflect the court's reputation, though the focus on governance leaves less energy for military innovation.

destiny.name: Grand Market of the Sahel
destiny.text: Transform the Mossi realm into the premier trading power of the Sahel. Bring gold to the capital markets, raise Ouagadougou to twice its old size, and secure the southern trade hub of Kong.

conditions.text: The capital

children.text: Gold is produced in the market
Gold is traded in the market

Own Kong, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75

event.title: The Golden Age of Mossi
event.text: Gold flows through our capital markets. The trade hub of Kong connects our realm to the wealth of the forest kingdoms. Ouagadougou has become the market where the Sahel and the forest meet. The Mogho Naba presides over a realm that would astonish the founding ancestors, not because it was won by the sword, but because it was built by the steady application of naam's wisdom to the challenges of governance and commerce. The Mossi model, stability through sacred hierarchy, prosperity through controlled trade, stands as a beacon for the Sahel.

options.text: Let Mossi prosperity light the way forward.

modifiers.name: Sahel Golden Age
modifiers.text: An era of unprecedented prosperity transforms the Mossi heartland. Cities grow, roads connect markets, and the people feel a profound satisfaction with their ruler's stewardship.

options.text: The naam endures, a legacy for all ages.

modifiers.name: Naam Legacy
modifiers.text: The enduring legacy of naam governance ensures stability across generations. Neighboring peoples view the Mossi with respect rather than fear, and the nobility stands as a pillar of the realm.

units.name: Nakomsé Horsemen
units.text: The mounted warriors of the Mossi ruling class, whose cavalry tradition stretches back to the founding ancestors who rode north from Mamprusi. Armed with spears and fighting from horseback across the open grasslands, they are the embodiment of naam power.

units.name: Mossi Lancers
units.text: Professional cavalry armed with iron-tipped lances forged by Mossi blacksmiths. These mounted warriors combine the traditional Nakomsé riding skill with heavier armament, forming the striking arm of Mossi armies.

units.name: Talse Bowmen
units.text: The commoners of the villages, called out on foot with bows and poisoned arrows. They follow the noble horse and hold what it has taken.

units.name: Mossi Iron Guard
units.text: Heavy infantry equipped with superior weapons and armor from the feared Mossi blacksmith lineages. These soldiers hold the line while the cavalry maneuvers, their iron shields and blades a testament to the skill of the forge.

units.name: Sahel Riders
units.text: Mounted warriors adapted to the full spectrum of Sahel terrain, from the open grasslands to the scrubland edges of the desert. Fast-moving and tactically flexible, they excel at flanking maneuvers and rapid raids.

units.name: Naam Cavalry
units.text: The last evolution of the Nakomsé mounted tradition, combining centuries of grassland horsemanship with modern tactical discipline. Raised through the levy system from noble families who carry the naam, they fight for divine right as much as for territory.

units.name: Ouidi Riders
units.text: Horsemen kept under arms the year round by the Ouidi Naba, the minister of the cavalry. They are drilled as one body and still ride with the lance.

buildings.name: Naba's Court
buildings.text: The administrative complex of a Mossi naba, where the chief holds court surrounded by his ministers and servants. Provincial courts mirror the structure of the Mogho Naba's own palace in Ouagadougou, creating a chain of governance from capital to village.

buildings.name: Earth Shrine
buildings.text: A sacred grove tended by the tengsoba earth priest, where offerings are made to the spirits of the land. These ancient shrines predate Mossi political authority and remain essential to agricultural fertility and community cohesion.

buildings.name: Mossi Forge
buildings.text: A workshop operated by the feared blacksmith lineages of the Mossi, who hold the dangerous and powerful knowledge of iron smelting. Their forges produce the weapons, tools, and implements that sustain both the military and agricultural life of the kingdom.

buildings.name: Sahel Caravanserai
buildings.text: A fortified rest station along the trade routes, offering shelter, water, and markets for the caravans that carry salt, kola nuts, cotton, and livestock across the Sahel.

buildings.name: Weaving House
buildings.text: A workshop where Mossi men work the narrow strip looms, weaving cotton thread spun and dyed by women into the long strips that are sewn together into robes and trade cloths.

buildings.name: Zai Fields
buildings.text: Before the rains, pits are dug into hard and crusted ground and a handful of manure is laid in each. The first storm fills them, and the millet is sown where the water stood.

buildings.name: Horse Stud
buildings.text: Herds of brood mares kept for the naba. Horses do not thrive far to the south, so every court of the Volta buys its mounts from studs such as this.

where.text: The location's raw material is Horses

buildings.name: Dolo House
buildings.text: A compound where the women brew dolo, the red millet beer. Neighbours gather under its shelter on market day.

buildings.name: Kimse Roogo
buildings.text: The house of the ancestors of a lineage. Its masks are kept here between funerals, and the elder brings the offerings.

buildings.name: Mossi War Camp
buildings.text: A permanent military encampment where Nakomsé cavalry are trained, equipped, and mustered for the campaigns of conquest that have carried the Mossi banner from the Volta to the Niger. The camp's forges produce weapons while its corrals hold the finest cavalry mounts in the Sahel.

buildings.name: Mossi Grand Market
buildings.text: A sprawling commercial complex where traders from across the Sahel meet under the regulation and protection of the Mogho Naba's appointed market officials. Salt from the north, gold from the south, cloth from Mossi looms, and livestock from the grasslands change hands in an orderly exchange that enriches all participants.

list.name: Nayiri Council of the Five Naabas
list.text: The electoral and advisory council of the Mogho Naaba, drawn since the founding of Wagadugu from five palace ministers: the Baloum Naaba, head of the king's household; the Gounga Naaba, chief of infantry; the Larle Naaba, keeper of the royal tombs and customs; the Kamsaogo Naaba, manager of the palace eunuchs; and the Ouidi Naaba, royal groom and chief of cavalry, dean of the ministers. The council selected each new Mogho Naaba from the eligible sons of the late king, and could pass over an heir judged unfit for war or office. The same five offices governed the Yatenga court at Ouahigouya, and the council's veto over succession made it the institutional counterweight to the throne for the entire pre-colonial era.

list.name: Moro-Naba Friday Court
list.text: The weekly Naam-investiture audience at Wagadugu, attested in oral tradition since the foundation of the city and still performed at dawn every Friday in the modern era. The Mogho Naaba emerges from the palace dressed in red and seated on a horse as if for war; provincial chiefs, ministers, and lineage heads arrange themselves by rank in the courtyard; oaths of loyalty are renewed and grievances heard. The ritual is the institutional mechanism by which naam, the divine right to command, flows from the throne into every chieftaincy in the empire. No new village or provincial chief can rule without his naam being conferred at Wagadugu.

conditions.text: Owns Ouagadougou

list.name: Tengsoba Earth-Priest Compact
list.text: The dual settlement between the Mossi conquerors descending from the marriage of Princess Yennenga and the hunter Riale in the early thirteenth century and the autochthonous Voltaic peoples (Nyonyose, Kibsi, Doghosie) who held the land before them. Mossi political authority (naam) belongs to the nakomse; spiritual authority over the soil (tenga) belongs to the tengsoba earth-priest, always drawn from the autochthonous lineage. No field can be cleared, no village founded, no rain invoked, without the tengsoba's ritual sanction. The compact is the institutional basis of Mossi rural stability: it lets a thin warrior aristocracy govern a much larger conquered population without exterminating its religion.

list.name: Nakomse Provincial Governance
list.text: The patrilineal system through which the Mogho Naaba's sons (the Dimas) were assigned provinces, and nakomse cousins were appointed to lesser chieftaincies down the Mossi heartland. Each nakomse held his territory by hereditary right of conquest, owed cavalry service on royal summons, collected tribute through village chiefs, and forwarded a share to the throne. The system gave the empire its famed long-range cavalry (it was Mossi horsemen who raided Mali in 1328-1338 and turned back a Songhai expedition in 1483), but it also fed the centrifugal tendency that produced the rival kingdoms of Wagadugu, Yatenga, Tenkodogo, Fada N'Gourma, and (later) Boussouma.

list.name: Yarse Trade Charter
list.text: The institutional incorporation of the Yarse, Mande-speaking Muslim caravan-merchants descended from Dyula-Wangara traders who arrived in Mossi country in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. Granted formal residence rights in the late eighteenth century (some sources date a 1780 grant by Naaba Saaga), the Yarse ran quarters in Wagadugu, Kaya, Rakaye, and Patenga, paid trade fees to the throne, and dominated the long-distance kola-salt-textile circuit between the Akan forest at Salaga and the Niger bend at Timbuktu. Their endogamous merchant lineages preserved Islam and literacy at court without converting the throne, and provided the Mossi state with its most reliable source of cash revenue and its only window into the Sahelian Muslim political world.
